NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  CITY OF BELL CITY COUNCIL
  Application: Moratorium

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. the City
Council of the City of Bell will conduct a public hearing to consider a temporary moratorium on
the establishment of new Data Center land use applications in the City.

A moratorium will allow the City time to thoroughly review, study and, if necessary, revise the
City’s laws, rules, procedures, and fees related to Data Centers to enable the City to adequately
and appropriately balance the rights of any existing operators and future applicants who wish to
establish or expand Data Centers in the City with the preservation of the health, safety and welfare
of the community.

The term “Data Center” means any facility or structure whose sole or primary function is to house
servers and data storage systems with connections to the public internet or closed enterprise
networks for large scale software systems and the computational demands of traditional
computational demands and generative artificial intelligence. A Data Center may also include
backup power generators, water cooling and storage facilities, air handlers, utility substations, fire
suppression systems, and other infrastructure to support operations. The term “Data Center” does
not include: 1.) City actions; and 2.) Data processing facilities whose use is secondary or ancillary
to another expressly permitted use, located on less than one acre of land.”

All parties wishing to speak for or against the matter should attend the public hearing and express
their concerns on the proposed moratorium. Any person desiring to provide written comments on
this matter must do so prior to or at the Public Hearing. Written comments can be sent via U.S.
Mail, or by hand delivery, to the City Clerk, 6330 Pine Avenue, Bell, CA 90201, prior to said public
hearing. Written comments can also be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@cityofbell.gov. by
4:00 p.m. on Wednesday, October 14, 2026.

For further details, contact  Javier  Ochiqui,  Community  Development  Director,  at
jochiqui@cityofbell.gov

NOTICE IS FURTHER GIVEN that in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA), Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the
proposed ordinance amendment is exempt because there is no possibility that the activity may
have a significant effect on the environment.

If you wish to legally challenge any action taken by the City on the above matter, you may be
limited to raising only those issues you or someone else raised at the public hearing described in
this notice.

In the City’s efforts to comply with the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act, the City
requires that any person in need of any type of special equipment, assistance, or
accommodation(s) to communicate at the public hearing must inform City staff a minimum of 72
hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  CITY OF BELL CITY COUNCIL
  ALLEY VACATION

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. the City Council of the
City of Bell will conduct a public hearing at the Bell Community Center located at 6250 Pine Avenue, Bell,
CA 90201 in accordance with Streets and Highways Section 8320 to consider the vacation of a public alley
located on the subject property at 4210 East Gage Avenue. Specifically, it is a 10’-wide alley spanning east-
west from Otis Avenue to Fishburn Avenue that bisects the site approximately in half with the northern
parcels adjacent to Gage Avenue and the other parcels comprising the southern portion of the property.
The alley has a length of approximately 250 feet and has ingress and egress points at Otis and Fishburn
Avenues.

  Subject Area

All parties wishing to speak for or against the matter should attend the public hearing and express their
thoughts on the proposed project. Any person desiring to provide written comments on this matter must do
so prior to or at the Public Hearing. Written comments can be sent via U.S. Mail, or by hand delivery, to
the City Clerk, 6330 Pine Avenue, Bell, CA 90201, prior to said public hearing. For further details, contact
William Galvez, Deputy City Engineer, at wgalvez@cityofbell.org.
 In the City’s efforts to comply with the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act, the City requires
that any person in need of any type of special equipment, assistance, or accommodation(s) to communicate
at the public hearing must inform City staff a minimum of 48 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

   Welcome to the City Council Meeting
The Bell City Council and staff welcome you. This is your City Government.
Individual participation is a basic part of American Democracy and all Bell residents
are encouraged to attend meetings of the City Council. Regular City Council
meetings are held the second and fourth Wednesday of the month at 7:00 p.m.,
Bell Community Center, 6250 Pine Avenue. For more information, you may call
City Hall during regular business hours 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through
Friday at (323) 588-6211 Extension 2615.

  City Council Organization

There are five City Council members, one of whom serves as Mayor and is the
presiding officer of the City Council. These are your elected representatives who
act as a Board of Directors for the City of Bell. City Council members are like you,
concerned residents of the community who provide guidance in the operation of
your City.

  Addressing the City Council

If you wish to speak to the City Council on any item which is listed or not listed on
the City Council Agenda, please complete a Request to Speak Card available in
the back of the City Council Chambers. Please submit the completed card to the
City Clerk prior to the meeting. The Mayor will call you to the microphone at the
appropriate time if you have filled out a Request to Speak Card. At that time,
approach the podium and please clearly state your name and address, and
proceed to make your comments.

  Compliance with Americans with Disabilities Act

The City of Bell, in complying with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA),
request individuals who require special accommodation(s) to access, attend, and
or participate in a City meeting due to disability. Please contact the City Clerk’s
Office, (323) 588-6211, Ext. 2615, at least one business day prior to the scheduled
meeting to ensure that we may assist you.

  Statement Regarding Compensation for Members of the Bell City Council

Compensation for the members of the Bell City Council is $673 a month. In
accordance with Government Code Section 54952.3, Councilmembers will not
receive any additional compensation or stipend for the convening of the following
regular meetings: Successor Agency to the Bell Community Redevelopment
Agency, the Bell Community Housing Authority, the Bell Public Finance Authority,
the Bell Surplus Property Authority, and the Bell Solid Waste Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENT: Each City Council meeting agenda includes a Public Comment period, providing members of the public
with an opportunity to address the City Council on items listed on the agenda, as well as non-agenda matters that are within
the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and/or its related authorities and agencies.

Public Comment In-Person

Please complete a Request to Speak Card and submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the meeting. Speakers will be
called in the order in which Speaker Cards are received. When recognized by the Mayor, speakers should approach the podium,
state their name for the record, and address the City Council. Each speaker is allotted up to three (3) minutes and may speak
once during the Public Comment portion of the agenda.

Public Comment Remotely

The City provides remote participation through the Zoom audio communication platform. Members of the public may observe
the meeting and provide public comment by either:

  •  Calling the telephone number provided on the agenda; or
  •  Joining the Zoom meeting using the Meeting ID and Passcode listed on the agenda.

To provide public comment on Closed Session items, participants must call no later than 5:00 p.m. To provide public comment
on Regular Session items, participants must use the Raise Hand feature prior to the start of the meeting at 7:00 p.m.

During the Public Comment period, participants joining via Zoom must use the Raise Hand feature to request to speak.
Participants joining by telephone must press *9 to raise their hand. Requests to speak must be submitted before the meeting
begins. Individuals who join after the meeting has started will not be permitted to speak during Public Comment.

When the Mayor announces your name or phone number, you will be prompted to speak. At that time, please unmute your
microphone or telephone line, state your name for the record, and proceed with your comments.

Members of the public attending the meeting in person will be invited to speak first, followed by remote participants. Remote
speakers will be recognized in the order their calls are received. Each remote speaker is allotted up to three (3) minutes to
address the City Council.

You may also submit input electronically through a temporary public comment email established for City of Bell City Council
meetings at cityclerk@cityofbell.org. Your written comment must be submitted by 4pm on Wednesday, October 14, 2026. Any
emails received after the time indicated will not be included in the record. Written Comments will be subject to the three minute
time limitation (approximately 350 words).

The meeting will be recorded and live streamed on the City’s website at https://www.cityofbell.gov/City-Hall/City-
Clerk/Live-Web-Stream

   RESOLUTION NO. 2026–61

  A RESOLUTION OF THE INTENT TO VACATE BY THE CITY
  OF BELL CITY COUNCIL TO APPROVE AN ALLEY VACATION
  THAT IS LOCATED IN THE CENTER OF THE ENTIRE
  PROPERTY AND EXTENDS ACROSS ITS ENTIRE LENGTH
  THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS LOCATED AT 4210 EAST GAGE
  AVENUE

  WHEREAS, LA Promise Fund/Option for Youth (“the Applicant”), filed a complete
application requesting the approval of an Alley Vacation for the alley at 4210 E. Gage Avenue
described herein (“Application”); and

  WHEREAS, the Application pertains to an approximate 50,820 square-foot property with
Los Angeles County Assessor’s Parcel Numbers 6325-009-002, 6325-009-003, 6325-009-004,
6325-009-005, 6325-009-006, 6325-009-007, more commonly known as 4210 Gage Avenue,
Bell California (“Property”);

  WHEREAS, the Applicant requests approval of an alley vacation to establish (permit) a
public charter high school (grades 9-12). Pursuant to the City of Bell Municipal Code (BMC)
Section 17.96.030(78)(a-d), “schools, charter, vocational, public” shall be permitted with the
approval of a CUP; and

  WHEREAS, the City staff reviewed the project’s environmental impacts under the
California Environmental Quality Act (California Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq.,
“CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 California Code of Regulations §§
15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”) and determined that the project is exempt under a Class
1 Categorical Exemption pursuant to section 15301(a) (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA
Guidelines (Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations); and

  WHEREAS, notice of the Planning Commission public hearing of September 2, 2026,
was published in compliance with State law in a local newspaper of general circulation. In
addition, a public notice was mailed 10 days in advance of the hearing to each property owner,
occupants and resident within a 300-foot radius of the project site, indicating the date and time
of the public hearing in accordance with California Government Code 65091; and

  WHEREAS, on September 2, 2026, the Planning Commission held a public hearing to
receive public testimony and other evidence regarding the Application, including without
limitation, information provided to the Planning Commission by City staff and public testimony;
and

  WHEREAS, this Resolution and its findings are made based upon evidence presented
to the Commission at its public hearing including, without limitation, the staff report submitted by
the Community Development Department; and

  WHEREAS, all legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Resolution have been met.

  Resolution 2026-61
  Page 1  11
 NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BELL DOES HEREBY FIND,
DETERMINE AND DECLARE AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1. All of the facts set forth in the recitals are true and correct and are incorporated
herein by reference.

SECTION 2. Based upon substantial evidence presented to this Planning Commission during
the public hearing conducted with regard to the Application, including written staff reports, verbal
testimony, site plans, and Conditions of Approval (“Conditions”) attached hereto as Exhibit “A,”
the Planning Commission hereby specifically finds as follows:

A. The site for the proposed use is adequate in size, shape and topography to accommodate
  the proposed use. The site is developed with an existing two-story building with multiple staff
  offices, restrooms, and storage facilities previously occupied by a vocational school. The
  proposed high school will occupy the existing building without needing tenant improvements.
  The existing site is predominantly flat and contains parking areas and landscaping planters.
  Therefore, the existing building and site are adequate in size, shape, and topography to
  accommodate the proposed high school operations.

B. The site has sufficient access to public streets and highways adequate in width and
  pavement type, to carry the quantity and quality of vehicular and pedestrian traffic expected
  to be generated by the proposed use. The proposed parking layout on the site will provide
  58 parking spaces for faculty, staff, and students. Since the majority of students will take
  classes online, and only 30-50 students on site at a single time, staff anticipates this amount
  of parking will satisfy the needs of the people who are on the site.

C. All buildings and structures proposed to be constructed or utilized in conjunction with the
  use will be architecturally compatible with existing and prospective uses of land located in
  the immediate vicinity of the site. Since taking over the building the operator has repaired
  and/or replaced all the vandalized doors and windows. The applicant has patched and
  painted the damaged wall areas be as needed to match the unaffected wall areas. In
  addition, the applicant washed or repainted the building facades to eliminate dust and
  watermarks. Lastly, the applicant removed all unpermitted vinyl graphics and banners
  throughout the site. The applicant regularly maintains the cleanliness and appearance of the
  site, therefore, the use will not adversely impact the subject site or surrounding area.

D. The location of the proposed use on the site will be compatible with existing and prospective
  uses of land located in the immediate vicinity of the site. The site was previously re-
  developed with an educational facility, and no tenant improvements or additions to the
  building’s square feet are being proposed. In addition, the site has been previously occupied
  by other similar uses, including a vocational school, which has some similar operating
  characteristics of class settings and offices that are compatible with the existing surrounding
  commercial and residential land uses within the immediate vicinity.

E. The conduct of the proposed use will be in compliance with the City’s General Plan. The
  subject site’s General Plan Land Use Designations are Commercial and Medium Density
  Residential. The high school uses allowable within all zoning districts of the City, subject to
  the approval of a CUP. Therefore, with the approval of a CUP, the proposed high school use

   will be in compliance with the Zoning Code requirements and the City’s General Plan. The
  proposed land use will address the current and future needs of the residential sector by
  providing an educational facility for children residing within the surrounding residential areas.
  Therefore, the proposed project satisfies the Land Use and Sustainability Element Policy 1
  of the General Plan.

SECTION 3. The City Council reviewed the project’s environmental impacts under the
California Environmental Quality Act (California Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq.,
“CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 California Code of Regulations §§
15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”) and finds the project to be exempt under a Class 1
Categorical Exemption pursuant to section 15301(a) (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA
Guidelines (Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations); and

SECTION 4. The Planning Commission hereby approves ENT-7 subject to the execution and
fulfillment of Conditions of Approval set forth in Exhibit “A” attached to this Resolution.

SECTION 5. That the City Clerk shall certify to the passage and adoption of this Resolution
and enter it into the book of original Resolutions.

   ORDINANCE NO. 1299

  AN INTERIM URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF BELL
  PROHIBITING THE ESTABLISHMENT, RELOCATION, OR
  EXPANSION OF DATA CENTERS WITHIN CITY LIMITS DURING
  THE PENDENCY OF THE CITY’S REVIEW AND ADOPTION OF
  PERMANENT ZONING REGULATIONS FOR SUCH USES

THE BELL CITY COUNCIL DOES ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  WHEREAS, the City of Bell (“City”) has the authority, under its police powers, to enact
regulations for the public peace, safety, and general welfare of the City pursuant to its Charter
and California Constitution Article XI, section 7; and

  WHEREAS, the City has a compelling interest in protecting the public health, safety, and
welfare of its citizens, residents, visitors, and businesses, and in preserving the peace and quiet
of the neighborhoods within the City by regulating the establishment, expansion, and relocation
of Data Centers (as defined below) within City limits; and

  WHEREAS, the City is responsible for adopting and implementing land use regulations
within its boundaries; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Bell Municipal Code (“BMC”) does not presently define “Data
Center” and contains no other development standards or regulations applicable to Data Center
land uses, including location, size, and scope; and

  WHEREAS, communities throughout the state and country have experienced detrimental
effects of Data Center land uses, including but not limited to intensive energy and water use,
noise, crime and security issues, air quality, water and noise pollution, aesthetic impacts, and
other related effects on property values and quality of life to surrounding neighborhoods; and

  WHEREAS, it is in the City’s best interest to promote orderly growth and balance the
development of Data Centers with respect to economics, compatibility with other uses, and
aesthetics; and

  WHEREAS, Government Code Sections 36934, 36937, and 65858 expressly
authorize the City Council to adopt an interim urgency ordinance for the immediate
preservation of the public peace, health or safety and to prohibit a use that is in conflict with
a contemplated general plan, specific plan, or zoning proposal that the legislative body,
Planning Commission, or the Planning Division is considering or studying or intends to study
within a reasonable time; and

  WHEREAS, City staff require time to study and develop appropriate zoning
appropriate regulations concerning the establishment, placement, and possible operational
conditions of Data Center land uses that are consistent with state and federal law; and

  WHEREAS, the City posted and published notice of the public hearing for this Ordinance
on September 30, 2026; and

01135.0001 2199680.2 Page 1 of 6

  22
   WHEREAS, pursuant to the above-described express statutory authority and its
police powers, the City Council desires, on an urgency basis, to temporarily prohibit
establishment of new, or the expansion or relocation of existing, Data Centers within the City.

NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BELL, CALIFORNIA, DOES
ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1.  FINDINGS

  The City Council finds the facts set forth in the recitals in this Ordinance are true and
correct and are hereby incorporated by reference. Additionally, based on the foregoing, both
verbal and written testimony at the public hearing, including the staff report, exhibits, and any
materials provided by members of the public, the City Council finds as follows:

  A.  Data Centers are currently undefined in the City’s Municipal Code, and the City
does not presently have adequate regulations governing the location, size, scope, development
standards, and operational conditions applicable to Data Centers. The City is currently studying
new zoning regulations for these uses. The City Council is adopting this Ordinance in order to
allow the City time to thoroughly study and develop the City’s laws, rules, procedures, and
potential fees related to the development, operation, and establishment of Data Centers to enable
the City to adequately and appropriately preserve the health, safety, and welfare of residents in
the City.

  B.  For the purposes of this Ordinance, the term “Data Center” shall mean and include:
(i) any facility or structure whose sole or primary function is to house servers and data storage
systems with connections to the public internet or closed enterprise networks for large-scale
software systems and the computational demands of traditional computing and generative
artificial intelligence; and (ii) backup power generators, water cooling and storage facilities, air
handlers, utility substations, fire suppression systems, and other infrastructure used to support
Data Center operations. The term “Data Center” shall not include: (i) actions undertaken by the
City; or (ii) data processing facilities whose use is secondary or ancillary to another expressly
permitted use and that are located on less than one acre of land.

  C.  For the purposes of this Ordinance, the term “Data Center operator” shall mean a
person that owns, manages, and/or operates a Data Center.

  D.  The City Council finds that, in the absence of a sufficient regulatory framework
governing Data Centers, the establishment or expansion of Data Centers may result in significant
adverse impacts on the public health, safety, and welfare of the community, including impacts
associated with intensive energy and water use, noise, air quality, water and noise pollution,
security, aesthetics, property values, quality of life, and demands on existing utility infrastructure.

  E.  The City Council finds that the potential adverse impacts from Data Centers
include the following:

  1. Data Centers are not presently subject to adequate City regulation or oversight concerning
  their location, size, scope, development standards, and operational conditions;

01135.0001 2199680.2 Page 2 of 6

  23
   2. Data Centers may involve intensive energy and water consumption and may require
  unique or abnormally large connections to electrical, water, and sewage infrastructure,
  potentially exceeding the capacity of existing infrastructure or placing significant demands
  on those systems;

  3. Data Centers and their associated backup generators and heating, ventilation, and air
  conditioning systems may generate substantial and continuous noise that can adversely
  affect surrounding properties and residents;

  4. Data Centers may result in impacts related to air quality, water and noise pollution,
  security, aesthetics, property values, and the quality of life of surrounding neighborhoods;
  and

  5. The continued establishment or expansion of Data Centers before the City has completed
  its study and adopted appropriate regulations may result in development that is
  inconsistent with regulations concerning the location, size, scope, development standards,
  or operational conditions of Data Centers that the City is currently considering.

  F.  The City needs time to study the relevant issues and draft proposed amendments
to the City’s zoning regulations in order to appropriately regulate the establishment, placement,
development, expansion, and operation of Data Centers and preserve the health, safety, and
welfare of the community.

SECTION 2.  CEQA COMPLIANCE

  Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act Guidelines ("CEQA," California Code
of Regulations Title 14, §§ 15000 et seq.), this Ordinance is exempt from CEQA based on the
following: (i) this Ordinance is not a “project” within the meaning of CEQA Section 15378 because
it has no potential for resulting in physical change to the environment, either directly or indirectly;
and (ii) this Ordinance is also exempt pursuant to CEQA Section 15061(b)(3) because it merely
establishes a 45-day temporary moratorium on the establishment and expansion of Data Centers,
and thus there is no possibility that this Ordinance may have a significant effect on the
environment.

SECTION 3.  AUTHORITY AND EFFECT

  The State Planning and Zoning Law (Cal. Gov’t Code Sections 65000, et seq.) and the
City’s Charter broadly empower the City to plan for and regulate the use of land in order to provide
for orderly development, the public health safety and welfare, and a balancing of property rights
and the desires of the community and the manner in which its citizens envision their city.

SECTION 4.  MORATORIUM

  A.  The “Effective Period” of this Ordinance shall be forty-five (45) days following
adoption (unless extended pursuant to Government Code Section 65858). During the Effective
Period, no permit shall be issued for the development, establishment, or operation of any new
Data Center, nor may a permit be issued for the expansion of an existing Data Center, in the City.
01135.0001 2199680.2 Page 3 of 6

  24
 The foregoing shall explicitly prohibit the approval or issuance of any subdivision, use permit,
variance, site plan and design review, development and site plan review, zoning compliance
review, grading permit, building permit, or any other entitlement, including the issuance of a
business license, for any new Data Center or the expansion of any existing Data Center.

  B.  Notwithstanding the foregoing, any existing Data Center shall be allowed to obtain
its annual City business license. Additionally, permits may be issued for minor construction,
rehabilitation, landscaping, or other purposes not involving an expansion of building area,
provided such work does not increase the floor area or intensity of use of the Data Center. Any
Data Center under construction with a valid building permit, any Data Center that obtained
administrative planning approval with the concurrence of the City Manager or his/her designee,
or any Data Center approved by the Planning Commission as of the effective date of this
Ordinance shall be exempt from the moratorium established by this Ordinance.

SECTION 5.  STUDY AND DEVELOPMENT

  During the Effective Period of this Ordinance, the City shall study and develop as
necessary City laws, rules, procedures, and fees related to Data Centers to enable the City to
adequately and appropriately preserve the health, safety, and welfare of the community in the
City. Pursuant to Government Code Section 65858, the Community Development Director will
issue a report for the City Council on what has been accomplished during the Effective Period.

SECTION 6.  URGENCY MEASURE

  It is hereby declared that this Ordinance is necessary as an urgency measure for the
immediate preservation of public peace, health, safety, and welfare. The City Council finds that
its current zoning regulations and land use plans do not adequately regulate the development,
establishment, and operation of Data Centers, and therefore do not adequately protect the peace,
health, safety, and general welfare of the residents of the City or communities around the City.
The City Council finds that this urgency measure is necessary in order to ensure adequate
regulation of the development and operation of Data Centers. The facts constituting the urgency
are:

  A.  The City does not currently have sufficient standards in the BMC related
specifically to the development, establishment, expansion, and operation of Data Centers within
the City. Data Centers may result in significant impacts related to energy and water consumption,
utility infrastructure, noise, air quality, security, aesthetics, property values, and quality of life.
Approval of a Data Center project without sufficient regulation may therefore result in significant
negative impacts upon the public health, safety, and welfare of the community.

  B.  The City is in the preliminary stages of reviewing its zoning regulations to
determine whether additional standards are necessary to address the potentially detrimental
impacts of Data Centers. Such uses, if not sufficiently regulated constitute a current and
immediate threat to the public health, safety, and welfare. Examples of potential impacts
generated by these uses include the following, which require greater study and evaluation:

01135.0001 2199680.2 Page 4 of 6

  25
   1. Significant energy and water consumption and the need for unique or abnormally large
  connections to electrical, water, and sewage infrastructure, which may place substantial
  demands on existing utility systems;
  2. Substantial and continuous noise generated by Data Center operations and associated
  equipment, including backup generators and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning
  systems, which may adversely affect surrounding properties and residents; and
  3. Impacts related to air quality, water and noise pollution, security, aesthetics, property
  values, and the quality of life of surrounding neighborhoods.

  C.  Data Center operators may seek to establish or expand Data Centers in locations,
concentrations, or development patterns that are inconsistent with regulations concerning the
location, size, scope, development standards, and operational conditions of Data Centers that the
City is currently studying. Permitting such development to proceed before the City completes its
study and adopts appropriate regulations may frustrate the purpose of those regulations and
further exacerbate the potential impacts identified above.

  As a result of the potential negative and harmful effects associated with insufficiently
regulated development and operation of Data Centers, it is necessary to adopt a temporary, forty-
five (45) day moratorium on the establishment of new Data Centers and the expansion of existing
Data Centers in the City.

  The moratorium established by this Ordinance will allow the City sufficient time to conclude
its studies and the preparation of appropriate zoning regulations governing such activities.

SECTION 7.  SEVERABILITY

  The City Council hereby declares that if any provision, section, subsection, paragraph,
sentence, phrase, or word of this Ordinance is rendered or declared invalid or unconstitutional by
any final action in a court of competent jurisdiction or by reason of any preemptive legislation,
then the City Council would have independently adopted the remaining provisions, sections,
subsections, paragraphs, sentences, phrases, or words of this Ordinance, and as such they shall
remain in full force and effect.

SECTION 8.  EFFECTIVENESS OF ORDINANCE.

  This Ordinance shall take effect immediately upon its adoption by a 4/5 vote of the City
Council, pursuant to the authority conferred upon the City Council by Government Code Section
65858. This Ordinance shall be effective during the Effective Period, which shall be from its
adoption and shall be of no further force and effect forty-five (45) days following the date of its
adoption, unless extended in accordance with the provisions set forth in Government Code
Section 65858(b).

SECTION 9.  PUBLICATION

  The City Clerk shall certify as to the passage and adoption of this Ordinance and shall
cause the same to be published in a manner prescribed by law.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the City of Bell (“City”) is requesting proposals from qualified

services in support of the City’s Public Works Department. Services will be provided on an as-
needed basis through individually issued task orders or requests for quotes for specific projects.

  SCOPE OF SERVICES

  I. Consultant will perform the following services on an on-call basis:

  1. Staff Augmentation;
  2. Project Management; and
  3. Construction Management and Inspection.

  No staff substitution is allowed without a written approval from the City. Consultant is expected to
  monitor their approved budget and notify the City of any work that is outside the Scope of Services
  prior to performing additional work.

  1. Staff Augmentation

  The Consultant shall provide on-call services to augment City Engineering staff through program
  management and payment support services related to the City’s Capital Improvement Program
  (“CIP”), which shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

  •  Perform Plan checks for CIP;
  •  Perform land development projects review;
  •  Coordinate with Planning Department and prepare Condition of Approval for projects;
  •  Prepare City Council Reports;
  •  Consultant contract management;
  •  Issue Public Works Permits (Construction and Encroachment);
  •  Administration of public works contracts, including preparation of RFPs, addendums, and related
  documents;
  •  Coordinate vendor solicitations, prepare bid packages, and evaluate proposals;
  •  Right-of-Way acquisition, coordination, and support services;
  •  Perform reference checks and prepare recommendations for contract award;
  •  Organize and participate in project progress meetings, including preparation of and distribution of
  minutes;
  •  Coordinate and schedule required inspections, surveys, and geotechnical tests;
  •  Monitor and review design consultant’s progress, budget and schedule, review plans, and technical
  specifications for completeness and constructability;
  •  Prepare technical reports; and
  •  Conduct technical research, data collection, and analysis to support project delivery.

  2. Project Management

  The Public Works Director will serve as the contract manager and direct liaison between the
  Consultant and Caltrans District #7 Division of Local Assistance. The Consultant shall be
  responsible for project management activities throughout the Term of this Agreement and the scope
  of activities includes, but is not limited to, coordinating and being responsible for scheduling
  meetings, managing the project schedule, preparing and distributing minutes, field reviews,
  tracking action items for the City and consultant sub-contractors, and preparing all submissions
  for the City to submit to Caltrans Local Assistance.

01135.0006 2194143.3 9/28/2026  A-1

  115
   Consultant shall ensure all work conforms with applicable City, state and federal Laws, latest
  versions of City Design Manuals, City Standard Plans, Caltrans Manual and Policies, Caltrans
  Standard Plans and specifications, APWA Standard Drawings and Standard Specifications for
  Public Works.

  3. Construction Management and Inspection

  Consultant shall provide construction management and inspection services on CIP projects
  including street improvements, bike paths, drainage improvements, parks, buildings, open space
  amenities, landscaping, traffic signals, sewer and underground construction. Consultant shall
  provide experienced personnel to perform the following tasks:

  •  Provide Full time inspection for construction activities
  •  Prepare daily project tracking documentation such as daily report logs, and digital photos
  •  Monitor construction project progress and pay reports. Review Contractor’s payment
  request and make recommendations for payment
  •  Review, and make recommendations for change orders
  •  Review and respond to Request For Information (RFI’s)
  •  Provide and maintain logs for RFIs, change orders, submittals, and related construction
  document
  •  Coordinate with Utility Companies
  •  Monitor, evaluate, and report contractor’s labor compliance
  •  Monitor, evaluate, and report contractor’s environmental compliance, including preparing
  the Stormwater Multiple Application and Report Tracking System (SMARTS) reports and
  updates, and uploading them into the online database
  •  Review contractor’s safety program
  •  Provide Construction General Permit Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) and/or
  Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD) support
  •  Prepare and monitor project punch-list
  •  Issue correction notices for deficiencies found, and monitor and enforce all corrective
  action as necessary
  •  Obtain all record (As-Built) drawings
  •  Prepare project and construction management procedures manual
  •  Host partnering sessions with the Construction Contract
  •  Prepare and process project closeout
  •  Document potential contractor claims and respond to contractor potential claim
  correspondence citing specific contract documents, and codes
  •  Prepare analysis of potential claims and make recommendations regarding their
  settlement
  •  Negotiate with contractor and assist the City to facilitate claim resolution

  SCOPE OF SERVICES

  I. Consultant will perform the following services on an on-call basis:

  1. Staff Augmentation
  2. Project Management
  3. Construction Management and Inspection
  4. Civil Engineering
  5. Traffic Engineering
  6. As-Needed Engineering Services

  No staff substitution is allowed without a written approval from the City. Consultant is expected to
  monitor their approved budget and notify the City of any work that is outside the Scope of Services
  prior to performing additional work.

  1. Staff Augmentation
  The Consultant shall provide on-call services to augment City Engineering staff through program
  management and payment support services related to the City’s Capital Improvement Program
  (CIP), which shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

    Perform Plan checks for CIP;
    Perform land development projects review;
    Coordinate with Planning Department and prepare Condition of Approval for projects;
    Prepare City Council Reports;
    Consultant contract management;
    Issue Public Works Permits (Construction and Encroachment);
    Administration of public works contracts, including preparation of RFPs, addendums, and
  related documents;
    Coordinate vendor solicitations, prepare bid packages, and evaluate proposals;
    Right-of-Way acquisition, coordination, and support services;
    Perform reference checks and prepare recommendations for contract award;
    Organize and participate in project progress meetings, including preparation of and distribution
  of minutes;
    Coordinate and schedule required inspections, surveys, and geotechnical tests;
    Monitor and review design consultant’s progress, budget and schedule, review plans, and
  technical specifications for completeness and constructability;
    Prepare technical reports; and
    Conduct technical research, data collection, and analysis to support project delivery.

  2. Project Management
  The Public Works Director will serve as the contract manager and direct liaison between the
  consultant and Caltrans District #7 Division of Local Assistance. The Consultant shall be
  responsible for project management activities throughout the life of the contract and the scope
  of activities includes, but is not limited to, coordinating and being responsible for scheduling
  meetings, managing the project schedule, preparing and distributing minutes, field reviews,

01135.0006 2194294.1 9/14/2026  A-1
  145
   tracking action items for the City and consultant sub-contractors, and preparing all submissions
  for the City to submit to Caltrans Local Assistance.
  Consultant shall ensure all work conforms with applicable City, state and federal laws, latest
  versions of City Design Manuals, City Standard Plans, Caltrans Manual and Policies, Caltrans
  Standard Plans and specifications, APWA Standard Drawings, and Standard Specifications for
  Public Works.

  3. Construction Management and Inspection
  Consultant shall provide construction management and inspection services on CIP projects
  including street improvements, bike paths, drainage improvements, parks, buildings, open space
  amenities, landscaping, traffic signals, sewer, and underground construction. Consultant shall
  provide experienced personnel to perform the following tasks:

    Provide full time inspection for construction activities;
    Prepare daily project tracking documentation such as daily report logs, and digital photos;
    Monitor construction project progress and pay reports. Review Contractor’s payment request
  and make recommendations for payment;
    Review, and make recommendations for change orders;
    Review and respond to Request for Information (RFIs);
    Provide and maintain logs for RFIs, change orders, submittals, and related construction
  document
    Coordinate with utility companies;
    Monitor, evaluate, and report contractor’s labor compliance;
    Monitor, evaluate, and report contractor’s environmental compliance, including preparing the
  Stormwater Multiple Application and Report Tracking System (SMARTS) reports and
  updates, and uploading them into the online database;
    Review contractor’s safety program;
    Provide Construction General Permit Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) and/or Qualified
  SWPPP Developer (QSD) support;
    Prepare and monitor project punch-list;
    Issue correction notices for deficiencies found, and monitor and enforce all corrective action as
  necessary;
    Obtain all record (As-Built) drawings;
    Prepare project and construction management procedures manual;
    Host partnering sessions with the City’s construction contractor;
    Prepare and process project closeout;
    Document potential contractor claims and respond to contractor potential claim
  correspondence citing specific contract documents and codes’
    Prepare analysis of potential claims and make recommendations regarding their settlement;
  and
    Negotiate with contractor and assist the City to facilitate claim resolution.

  4. Civil Engineering
  The Consultant will provide comprehensive civil engineering services to support the City in
  planning, design, and implementation of public infrastructure and public facility projects.
  Services will encompass all aspects of project development, including conceptual design,
  detailed engineering, surveying, regulatory compliance, and construction support. The

01135.0006 2194294.1 9/14/2026  A-2
  146
   Consultant will integrate cost management, scheduling, quality assurance, and risk assessment
  into all phases of the work.

  The Scope of Services includes design engineering services for streets, signs and striping, bike
  trails, storm drains, storm drain channels, sewer, structural, and all related services. The
  Consultant shall also provide design and specifications for signing, striping, detour plans, and
  traffic control where required by the scope of work.
  Consultant shall provide qualified personnel, necessary equipment, and appropriate resources to
  support the following services:
    Develop Plans, Specifications, and Estimates (PS&E) for a variety of capital improvement
  projects, including streets, bicycle facilities, storm drain systems, and sewer infrastructure;
    Prepare technical studies and supporting documentation, including hydrologic and hydraulic
  analyses, as required for project design and compliance;
    Prepare and review regulatory documents in accordance with applicable requirements,
  including National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) reports, Water Quality
  Management Plans (WQMP), and Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP);
    Site planning/grading design;
    Structural engineering (retaining wall, footing design, and etc.);
    Signing and striping;
    ADA design and assessment;
    Construction support; and
    Provide record drawings.

  All designs shall be prepared and submitted in a manner that ensures a complete design approved
  by the City Engineer with no more than three plan check submittals. Consultant must be
  proactive and knowledgeable of all regulations required for project acceptance. Consultant shall
  be an advisor, advocate, and produce a product with the best interest intended for the City within
  the required schedule and project budget.

  5. Traffic Engineering
  The Consultant shall provide traffic engineering services in support of the City’s transportation
  and infrastructure projects. Services may include, but are not limited to:
    Preparation of traffic studies, including traffic impact analyses, circulation studies, and level of
  service (LOS) evaluations;
    Development of traffic control plans (TCPs) and detour plans for construction projects,
  maintenance activities, and City-sponsored events or special activities;
    Design and evaluation of signage, striping, and pavement markings;
    Traffic signal design, modification, and timing analysis;
    Speed studies, traffic counts, and traffic calming evaluations;
    Parking studies and assessments;
    Preparation of plans, specifications, and cost estimates (PS&E);
    Coordination with City staff, utility agencies, and other stakeholders; and
    Assistance with grant applications and supporting traffic data analysis.

  All services shall be performed in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal standards
  and guidelines.

  In compliance with all terms and conditions of this Agreement, Consultant shall provide those
services specified in the “Scope of Services” attached hereto as Exhibit “A” and incorporated herein by
this reference, which may be referred to herein as the “services” or “work” hereunder. As a material
inducement to the City entering into this Agreement, Consultant represents and warrants: a) it has the
qualifications, experience, and facilities necessary to properly perform the Services required under this
Agreement; b) all services set forth in the Scope of Services will be performed in a competent and
satisfactory manner; c) all materials used for services will be both of good quality as well as fit for the
purpose intended; and, d) Consultant shall follow the highest standards and practices in performing the
services required hereunder. Individual tasks under the Scope of Services shall be established on a per
project basis and as set forth in a task order issued by the City (each, a “Task Order”). Upon request by the
City, the Consultant shall provide a detailed task proposal, including pricing consistent with those hourly
rates as provided in Article II, below. Consultant shall not commence work until a Task Order is issued by
the City authorizing the Consultant to perform such work.

  1.2  Consultant’s Proposal.

  The Scope of Services shall include the scope of services or work included in Consultant’s proposal
or bid, which shall be incorporated herein by this reference as though fully set forth herein. In the event of
any inconsistency between the terms of such proposal or bid, and this Agreement, the terms of this

  1.4  California Labor Law.

  If the Scope of Services includes any “public work” or “maintenance work,” as those terms are
defined in California Labor Code section 1720 et seq. and California Code of Regulations, Title 8, Section
16000 et seq., and if the total compensation is $1,000 or more, Consultant shall pay prevailing wages for
such work and comply with the requirements in California Labor Code section 1770 et seq. and 1810 et
seq., and all other applicable laws, including the following requirements:

  (a)  Public Work. The Parties acknowledge that some or all of the work to be performed
under this Agreement is a “public work” as defined in California Labor Code Section 1720, and that this
Agreement is therefore subject to the requirements of Division 2, Part 7, Chapter 1 (commencing with
Section 1720) of the California Labor Code relating to public works contracts and the rules and regulations
established by the Department of Industrial Relations (“DIR”) implementing such statutes. The work
performed under this Agreement is subject to compliance monitoring and enforcement by the DIR.
Consultant shall post job site notices, as prescribed by regulation.

  (b)  Prevailing Wages. Consultant shall pay prevailing wages to the extent required by
California Labor Code Section 1771. Pursuant to California Labor Code Section 1773.2, copies of the
prevailing rate of per diem wages are on file at City Hall and will be made available to any interested party
on request. By initiating any work under this Agreement, Consultant acknowledges receipt of a copy of the
DIR determination of the prevailing rate of per diem wages, and Consultant shall post a copy of the same
at each job site where work is performed under this Agreement.

  (c)  Penalty for Failure to Pay Prevailing Wages. Consultant shall comply with and be
bound by the provisions of California Labor Code Sections 1774 and 1775 concerning the payment of
prevailing rates of wages to workers and the penalties for failure to pay prevailing wages. Consultant shall,
as a penalty to the City, forfeit two hundred dollars ($200) for each calendar day, or portion thereof, for
each worker paid less than prevailing rates as determined by the DIR for the work or craft in which the
worker is employed for any public work done pursuant to this Agreement by Consultant or by any
subconsultant.

  (d)  Payroll Records. Consultant shall comply with and be bound by the provisions of
Labor Code Section 1776, which requires Consultant and each subconsultant to: keep accurate payroll
records and verify such records in writing under penalty of perjury, as specified in Section 1776; certify
and make such payroll records available for inspection as provided by Section 1776; and inform the City of
the location of the records.

  (e)  Apprentices. Consultant shall comply with and be bound by the provisions of
California Labor Code Sections 1777.5, 1777.6, and 1777.7 and California Code of Regulations Title 8,

  SCOPE OF SERVICES

I. Consultant will perform the following services on an on-call basis:

  1. Staff Augmentation;
  2. Project Management;
  3. Construction Management and Inspection Services;
  4. Civil Engineering Services;
  5. Traffic Engineering;
  6. Surveying and Mapping;
  7. Landscape Architecture;
  8. Architectural Design;
  9. Environmental Compliance;
  10. Grant Administration; and
  11. As-Needed Engineering Services.

No staff substitution is allowed without a written approval from the City. Consultant is expected to monitor
their budget and notify the City of any work that is outside the Scope of Services prior to performing
additional work.

1. Staff Augmentation
The Consultant shall provide on-call services to augment City Engineering staff through program
management and payment support services related to the City’s Capital Improvement Program (CIP), which
shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

    Perform Plan checks for CIP;
    Perform land development projects review;
    Coordinate with Planning Department and prepare Condition of Approval for projects;
    Prepare City Council Reports;
    Consultant contract management;
    Issue Public Works Permits (Construction and Encroachment);
    Administration of public works contracts, including preparation of RFPs, addendums, and related
  documents;
    Coordinate vendor solicitations, prepare bid packages, and evaluate proposals;
    Right-of-Way acquisition, coordination, and support services;
    Perform reference checks and prepare recommendations for contract award;
    Organize and participate in project progress meetings, including preparation of and distribution of
  minutes;
    Coordinate and schedule required inspections, surveys, and geotechnical tests;
    Monitor and review design consultant’s progress, budget and schedule, review plans, and technical
  specifications for completeness and constructability;
    Prepare technical reports; and
    Conduct technical research, data collection, and analysis to support project delivery.

 2. Project Management
The Public Works Director will serve as the contract manager and direct liaison between the Consultant
and Caltrans District #7 Division of Local Assistance. The Consultant shall be responsible for project
management activities throughout the Term of this Agreement and the scope of activities includes, but is
not limited to, coordinating and being responsible for scheduling meetings, managing the project schedule,
preparing and distributing minutes, field reviews, tracking action items for the City and consultant sub-
contractors, and preparing all submissions for the City to submit to Caltrans Local Assistance.
Consultant shall ensure all work conforms with applicable City, state and federal laws, latest versions of City
Design Manuals, City Standard Plans, Caltrans Manual and Policies, Caltrans Standard Plans and
specifications, APWA Standard Drawings, and Standard Specifications for Public Works.

3. Construction Management and Inspection
Consultant shall provide construction management and inspection services on CIP projects including street
improvements, bike paths, drainage improvements, parks, buildings, open space amenities, landscaping,
traffic signals, sewer, and underground construction. Consultant shall provide experienced personnel to
perform the following tasks:

    Provide full time inspection for construction activities;
    Prepare daily project tracking documentation such as daily report logs, and digital photos;
    Monitor construction project progress and pay reports. Review Contractor’s payment request and
  make recommendations for payment;
    Review, and make recommendations for change orders;
    Review and respond to Request for Information (RFIs);
    Provide and maintain logs for RFIs, change orders, submittals, and related construction document
    Coordinate with utility companies;
    Monitor, evaluate, and report contractor’s labor compliance;
    Monitor, evaluate, and report contractor’s environmental compliance, including preparing the
  Stormwater Multiple Application and Report Tracking System (SMARTS) reports and updates,
  and uploading them into the online database;
    Review contractor’s safety program;
    Provide Construction General Permit Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) and/or Qualified
  SWPPP Developer (QSD) support;
    Prepare and monitor project punch-list;
    Issue correction notices for deficiencies found, and monitor and enforce all corrective action as
  necessary;
    Obtain all record (As-Built) drawings;
    Prepare project and construction management procedures manual;
    Host partnering sessions with the City’s construction contractor;
    Prepare and process project closeout;
    Document potential contractor claims and respond to contractor potential claim correspondence
  citing specific contract documents and codes;
    Prepare analysis of potential claims and make recommendations regarding their settlement; and
    Negotiate with contractor and assist the City to facilitate claim resolution.

4. Civil Engineering
The Consultant will provide comprehensive civil engineering services to support the City in planning,
design, and implementation of public infrastructure and public facility projects. Services will encompass

 all aspects of project development, including conceptual design, detailed engineering, surveying, regulatory
compliance, and construction support. The Consultant will integrate cost management, scheduling, quality

drains, storm drain channels, sewer, structural, and all related services. The Consultant shall also provide

    Develop Plans, Specifications, and Estimates (PS&E) for a variety of capital improvement

    Traffic signal design, modification, and timing analysis;
    Speed studies, traffic counts, and traffic calming evaluations;
    Parking studies and assessments;
    Preparation of plans, specifications, and cost estimates (PS&E);
    Coordination with City staff, utility agencies, and other stakeholders; and
    Assistance with grant applications and supporting traffic data analysis.

All services shall be performed in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal standards and
guidelines.

  SCOPE OF SERVICES

  I. Consultant will perform the following services on an on-call basis:

  A. Water Quality and National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Compliance
  Services.

  Consultant shall provide water quality and NPDES compliance services to support the City’s
  projects and regulatory requirements. Services may include, but are not limited to:

    Monitoring, evaluating, and documenting contractor compliance with environmental and
  stormwater regulations during construction activities;
    Preparation, review, and electronic submittal of required reports through the State Water
  Resources Control Board’s Stormwater Multiple Application and Report Tracking System
  (SMARTS);
    Review and comment on Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP) and Water
  Pollution Control Programs (WPCP);
    Provision of Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) and/or Qualified SWPPP Developer
  (QSD) services, as required;
    Conducting site inspections and preparing compliance reports in accordance with applicable
  permits;
    Development and implementation of Best Management Practices (BMPs) for erosion,
  sediment, and pollutant control;
    Coordination with regulatory agencies and support during inspections or audits; and
    Assistance with compliance related to municipal stormwater permits (MS4), as applicable.

  All services shall be performed in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal regulations.
  No staff substitution is allowed without a written approval from the City. Consultant is expected to
  monitor their approved budget and notify the City of any work that is outside the Scope of Services
  prior to performing additional work.

  II. Consultant must perform all on-call services in compliance with the following requirements:

  A. Each task shall be indicated by a written request (“Task Order”) produced by the Contract Officer
  with a description of the work to be performed, and the time desired for completion. All tasks
  shall be carried out in conformity with all provisions of this Agreement. The Task Order may
  take the form or title of a “Purchase Order.” In the event of a conflict between the provision of
  any Task Order and any term of this Agreement, the provisions of this Agreement shall prevail.

  B. Consultant must prepare a written description of the requested tasks including all components
  and subtasks; the costs to perform the task (“Task Budget”), using the itemized fees as set forth
  in Exhibit “C”; explain how the cost was determined; and, a schedule for completion of the task
  (“Task Completion Date”); which shall all collectively be referred to as the “Task Proposal”.

  C. Contract Officer shall in writing approve, modify or reject the Task Proposal, and may issue a
  Task Order.

The insurance policies are to contain, or be endorsed to contain, the following provisions:

Additional Insured Status
The City, its officers, officials, employees, and volunteers are to be covered as additional insureds on the
CGL policy with respect to liability arising out of work or operations performed by or on behalf of the
Consultant including materials, parts, or equipment furnished in connection with such work or operations.

least as broad as ISO Form CG 20 10 11 85 or if not available, through the addition of both CG 20 10, CG
20 26, CG 20 33, or CG 20 38; and CG 20 37 if a later edition is used).

Primary Coverage
For any claims related to this contract, the Consultant’s insurance coverage shall be primary and non-
contributory and at least as broad as ISO CG 20 01 04 13 as respects the City, its officers, officials,
employees, and volunteers. Any insurance or self-insurance maintained by the City, its officers, officials,
employees, or volunteers shall be excess of the Consultant’s insurance and shall not contribute with it. This
requirement shall also apply to any Excess or Umbrella liability policies.

Umbrella or Excess Policy
The Consultant may use Umbrella or Excess Policies to provide the liability limits as required in this
agreement. This form of insurance will be acceptable provided that all of the Primary and Umbrella or
Excess Policies shall provide all of the insurance coverages herein required, including, but not limited to,
primary and non-contributory, additional insured, Self-Insured Retentions (SIRs), indemnity, and defense
requirements. The Umbrella or Excess policies shall be provided on a true “following form” or broader
coverage basis, with coverage at least as broad as provided on the underlying Commercial General Liability
insurance. No insurance policies maintained by the Additional Insureds, whether primary or excess, and
which also apply to a loss covered hereunder, shall be called upon to contribute to a loss until the
Consultant’s primary and excess liability policies are exhausted.

Notice of Cancellation
Each insurance policy required above shall provide that coverage shall not be canceled, except with notice
to the City.

Consultant may acquire against the City by virtue of the payment of any loss under such insurance.
Consultant agrees to obtain any endorsement that may be necessary to affect this waiver of subrogation, but
this provision applies regardless of whether or not the City has received a waiver of subrogation
endorsement from the insurer.

and any policies, including Excess liability policies, may not be subject to a SIR or deductible that exceeds
